newsitem.title: USA: Urethane to give voting control to group.
newsitem.headline: Urethane to give voting control to group.

text.p: Urethane Technologies Inc said Tuesday it had signed a preference share agreement with Endeavour Capital Corp that will give the investment group voting control of Urethane.
The company, a specialty chemicals and polyurethane systems producer, said the agreement will allow Endeavour to invest up to $1.65 million in Urethane in exchange for convertible preferred stock.
The preference shares will be convertible to the equivalent of 80 percent of Urethane's outstanding common stock, it said, adding that it had about 12 million shares of common stock outstanding.
In November, Urethane reported a third quarter loss of $0.25 a share including discontinued operations, against a loss of $0.03 a year before.

"(Urethane) has been undergoing a period of extremely difficult operations," it said. "During the last twelve months, we have experienced a significant squeeze in our operating margins due to higher levels of competition and increasing raw materials prices.

"(Urethane's) problems can only be resolved with the support of our lenders, creditors and the assistance of Endeavour Capital," it added. "We believe that with this assistance, combined with the many positive steps we have already taken to reduce our cost structure and strengthen our business profile, UTI will continue to grow and develop."
Endeavour is based in New York.
